notes_for_developer: Re-plan against DevCommand's REAL recipe library/compiler (docs/issues-log.md #21). Header/footer are real Elementor Theme Builder templates (kit_id 6, templates 61/62) and are intentionally OMITTED from this blueprint - only the 6 body sections are compiled here.

Two of the four pre-approved recipe mappings did not survive contact with the REAL recipes.json and were changed (flagged prominently in the handback report): value_columns (card-grid-3col's card template only has {{item.title}}/{{item.body}} - no icon or lead-paragraph slot, so it can't carry this design's icon+italic-lead+body cards) and testimonials (testimonial-grid's card template only has {{item.quote}}/{{item.author}} - no thumbnail/bio/watch-button slots, so it can't carry video-testimonial cards or the separate pull quote). Both are escape-hatch sections instead, per the 'never force a bad match' rule.

Content strings are carried over from docs/evidence/flow-a/00-improvised-build/blueprint-improvised-after-fixes.json, which was already re-verified verbatim against figma/data.json's raw TEXT node characters (issue #17, 0 mismatches) - not re-typed from screenshots.

All content_source values are literal (no content.json refs) because tools/figma_html/run_devcommand_compiler.py does not pass --content to compile_html_blueprint.py; content.json was not created since nothing here needs it.

tools/figma_html/run_devcommand_compiler.py gained a 3rd shim (issue #22): figma/tokens.json's colors/spacing/radii/typography are shaped for the SCSS/ACF pipeline, not this compiler's schema, and would have silently resolved to none of the project's real colors. See that script's own docstring.

notes: No recipe fits: fuses a page-H1 (Freeman 70/70, colour-span 2nd sentence) + a real 2-slide Swiper carousel with dots generated from the actual slide count (hidden when both slides show at once on desktop - accepted decision) + a CTA button pair + a same-row browse link. media-slider (bare carousel, no heading/CTA slots) and hero-two-column/hero-centered (single static media, no repeater) each cover only part of this.
Card border (3px sky, r48) is visible on the RIGHT card only per Figma (1:95 hidden on the left) - reproduced as-is.
Stray 1px black stroke on node 1:113 (designer leftover) intentionally NOT reproduced.

Mobile order: heading, then stacked cards, then browse-link+dots row (dots right, via margin-left:auto), THEN the two CTA buttons full width stacked - reproduced via flex `order` in the 430px media query so DOM order (CTAs adjacent to heading) stays accessible/SEO-friendly while only the visual order flips.
1024px tablet step has no Figma frame - linear interpolation (documented), not measured.

content_source.heading: ABOUT MIZUHO AMERICA
content_source.body: Established in Boston, Massachusetts in 1993, Mizuho America is part of Mizuho Corporation, a global medical products company with more than a century of commitment to providing surgeons with meticulously crafted equipment for their OR needs. With deep expertise in neurosurgical products, Mizuho America has built a legacy of quality, reliability, and trusted partnership with healthcare professionals. From problem-solving instrument sets developed with clinical experts, to ongoing support of neurosurgeons every day, Mizuho America remains committed to solutions that can help facilitate greater control, precision, and efficiency during the procedure with the goal of better outcomes after.

notes: No recipe fits: a unique 'stat counter' shape (not hero/nav/card-grid/testimonial/faq/gallery/cta/footer) - each stat is a white shadow-offset panel drawn under a colour-alternating card, not a plain title+icon+body card.

Stat row centred (accepted decision, Figma has it off-centre 76px left / 204px right). Stat-number line-height corrected from Figma's literal 36px (ratio 0.5625 of the 64px font-size) to ~1.1 (accepted decision).
Stat labels left-aligned inside their cards (G6), with right padding on the card so long labels ('years serving the neurosurgery community') wrap inside the card instead of spilling past its edge.
Third stat reads '1000+' (no thousands separator) vs the second stat's '1,800+' - the inconsistency is reproduced verbatim per accepted decision (typos/inconsistencies entered as designed).
